classifiedBy: one rater (the Claude model that ran this experiment), from each run's diff, every attempt's agent and verified file, the final messages and the reasoning or progress messages in the session logs; the automatic readings were visible while classifying, so agreement is a consistency check, not an independent one

codebook.edit: the final edit, in the categories of results.json rules.edits
codebook.response: the final file's behaviour (the oracle's verdict, read by hand against the diff) and whether the rule is satisfied, in the categories responseOf uses
codebook.saidBehaviourChanges: said that adding the dependencies the rule names changes when or how the effect runs (or, in A, that the edit made does)
codebook.mentionedStale: said the effect kept or read an old value or function (the first render's)
codebook.mentionedLoopOrExtraRuns: said a fix would run the effect on every render, more often, or loop
codebook.mentionedResubscribe: A: said the edit unsubscribes and resubscribes
codebook.mentionedTdz: B: said validate is declared below the effects, or that listing it throws
codebook.mentionedMountOnlyOrTrigger: said an effect is meant to run once, or that a dependency is there as a trigger
codebook.mentionedReactDocs: cited React's documentation or its recommended pattern
codebook.consultedReactDocs: opened a react.dev page with a tool
codebook.mentionedKeystrokes: said a fix would act on every keystroke or while typing
codebook.namedResidualDifference: named a case where its own edit behaves differently from the original
codebook.lookedForTests: searched for or read test files
codebook.lookedUpstream: looked up the upstream project's history or a later version

b-claude-1.notes: Extracted the two JSON.stringify keys (as the help text says) and read validate through two Effect Events; said adding the dependencies would run the effects 'on every render' and 'whenever the user edits the time'. Changed the bounds check to read the keys so the compiler rule sees them used.

b-claude-2.notes: Removed both effects and adjusted state during render instead ('React's recommended pattern for adjusting state when a prop changes'), keyed on JSON.stringify of the bounds. Named one difference: on mount the error now shows in the first render.

b-claude-3.notes: Like b-claude-1: keys and Effect Events; 'validation would run on every keystroke and show "Please enter a valid time" while the user is still typing'. Tried WebFetch for the rule docs (refused).

b-claude-4.notes: Keys and Effect Events; searched a cached oxlint binary in ~/.npm/_npx with Grep to check the rules know useEffectEvent; suggested deriving the error during render as an option and explained why it changes one case. 293 s, close to Ultracite's 300 s timeout.

b-codex-1.notes: Attempt 1: keys, Effect Events, and the effects moved below validate (the compiler then reports a second set-state-in-effect, handed back as new). Attempt 2: replaced both effects with guarded render-time updates. Reasoning: 'Adding every dependency directly would trigger validation while typing'. Opened react.dev's useEffectEvent page; ran 69 in-memory behaviour comparisons.

b-codex-2.notes: Same two-step path as b-codex-1 (one shared Effect Event with a default argument, then one guarded render-time block). 'Adding every dependency directly would change when validation runs and could reset an edited time.'

b-codex-3.notes: Same two-step path; opened react.dev's useEffectEvent page; 'could validate on every keystroke and reset edited input when the bounds change'; ran 17 before/after checks.

b-codex-4.notes: Same two-step path; opened react.dev's useEffectEvent page; 'Adding every value to the dependency arrays would change when validation runs and could reset an edited time.'

c-claude-1.notes: Added loadChats (said it's a no-op after the first load); saved through an Effect Event keyed on a string of the message count and last id that the effect reads, so the compiler stops calling the triggers extra. 'typing in the prompt would trigger a save on every keystroke'; 'it could also loop forever'. Named the one case it no longer saves on (isGenerating going from undefined to false alone).

c-claude-2.notes: Two Effect Events: the initial load kept [] ('should run once on mount, not every time loadChats changes'), the save keyed on JSON.stringify of all three triggers. Called the message count and id 'the real triggers for the save'.

c-claude-3.notes: Added loadChats; listed saveCurrentChat and three trigger locals, and compared them with the last save's in a ref so a callback change alone doesn't save. Named a Strict Mode difference: the original saved twice on mount in development, this once. Tried npx -y oxlint@1.86.0 (refused).

c-claude-4.notes: Like c-claude-1 (loadChats added; Effect Event; a message-count:id key the effect reads); named the same undefined-to-false gap and argued it can't happen.

c-codex-1.notes: Added loadChats and saveCurrentChat to the arrays, and a ref holding the previous trigger values that returns early when only the callback changed: the effect now runs on every chat change and does nothing (26 effect runs against 10 in the oracle's stable mode). 'I'll keep the existing save triggers and add a guard so those extra effect runs don't change the behavior.'

c-codex-2.notes: Same ref guard as c-codex-1; searched the run dir for test and spec files (none). 'Adding saveCurrentChat directly would also trigger saves on prompt edits and adapter changes.'

c-codex-3.notes: Same ref guard; 'The save callback changes when the prompt changes, so adding it directly would trigger extra saves.'

c-codex-4.notes: The initial load through an Effect Event with []; the triggers memoised into one object (useMemo over the three values) passed to an Effect Event, the effect depending on that object. Opened react.dev's useEffectEvent and Removing Effect Dependencies pages.
